Customize appearance Key Price Levels | OneOption - Stocks & Options Trading Suite Is the safety net going to hold? At this stage we’ve formulated our longer-term market opinion. We’ve determined which stage of the bullish cycle we’re in, we’ve evaluated the price action and we’ve set our measured moves. The market is making higher highs and higher lows. The dips are brief and shallow. Our charts are clean and anything that we add to them is secondary. This is a very important point because we really don’t need anything more than we already have. In the chart below we would enter a long position, add on con�rmation and take gains near the dotted line. Wait for the next dip, enter on support and repeat. Your game plan is to buy dips and to take gains into strength. You might be thinking that there’s no way it could be this easy. I hope this prospect has your heart racing. This is when everything goes to shit for many traders. They add the 100-day moving average to the chart and the SPY touches it. In an instant they �ip from bullish to bearish. They dismiss all of the technicals that suggest a strong up trend. They ignore that the odds of a bounce are much higher than the odds of a breakdown. This time is “different” and they are convinced that a market correction is starting. I can’t explain why this happens, but I see it all of the time. Heed my warning. When you add indicators to a chart they often do more harm than good. Only add what you absolutely need and keep your charts clean. The tools I’m going to describe are self-ful�lling (they work because traders use them). These price levels in�uence behavior. AVWAPQ The green line in the chart below is the anchored volume weighted average price for the quarter (AVWAPQ). I anchor it to Triple Witching (3rd Friday in March, June, September and December) because that is when large trading institutions “roll” their positions. Since this anchor is something that I developed, I don’t believe that other traders use it. AVWAPQ is the performance benchmark for the index since the start of the quarter and I believe that institutional trading algorithms reference it. The end of the quarter is also when Asset Managers are most likely to rebalance for the next quarter. They will start window dressing before the actual end of the quarter because of settlement and they want to spread the order �ow out to reduce market impact when they enter. That’s my theory for placing the anchor at Triple Witching. After observing it for many quarters, I’ve found that price point to be relevant. A friend and fellow trader (Brian Shannon) got me interested in the concept. He wrote a book called Maximum Trading Gains With Anchored VWAP The premise is that Asset Managers use executing brokers like Citadel for large orders. Citadel executes the trade and they honor VWAP over a predetermined time period (it could be days or weeks). The Asset Manager doesn’t have to staff a trade desk and they feel that VWAP is a fair price. AVWAPQ resets every quarter and it will often be the �rst line of support. When the market dips, we want the move to stay fairly tight to the indicator. When it spends very little time below it relative to the time it spends above it, the dip will be brief and shallow. During a strong uptrend, it might only spend a few days below AVWAPQ. As soon as the market closes above it, we have our �rst con�rmation of support and we can buy the dip. We want immediate follow through and we want the market to start distancing itself from AVWAPQ. That would be a sign that buyers are interested. If we don’t get that follow through in a few days, we use a close below AVWAPQ as a stop. That is a fairly tight stop so our losses will be tiny. No harm, no foul. We are in a bullish market cycle and we can evaluate the next AVWAPQ cross. If the move back above it accelerates quickly and the market challenges the recent high from the start of the dip, it’s a sign that buyers are aggressive. That speed is critical because it indicates that buyers see this as an excellent opportunity. Remember, when one side or the other is aggressive, our odds of predicting price movement are high. On a breakout to a new relative high we would add to the position. Look at the chart below and pretend that AVWAPQ doesn’t exist. Focus on the market cycle, the price action and the measured moves. The market is making higher lows and higher highs. It is in an up trend and that is our primary observation. That move lower is just probing for support and that level is more likely to hold than it is to fail. How do I know that? Because the market is in an uptrend! Never lose sight of that. Buy when the market crosses back above AVWAPQ and watch for immediate follow through. Moving Averages For purposes of this course, I will use the term moving average (MA) instead of simple moving average. If I am referencing an exponential moving average I will use EMA and I don’t use it for long-term market analysis. Let’s discuss a major concept �rst. When the 50-day MA crosses the 200-day MA, a new market cycle begins. There’s nothing magical about these crosses, we are simply comparing the short-term price action to the long-term price action. When it is improving we are bullish and when it is deteriorating we are bearish. Golden Cross – The 50-day MA has closed above the 200-day MA. This marks the beginning of a bullish market cycle. Death Cross – The 50-day MA has closed below the 200-day MA. This marks the beginning of a bearish market cycle. The only thing signi�cant about the 50-day, 100-day or 200-day MA is that other traders have them on their daily charts. I don’t use these moving averages for any other time frame. The 200-day moving average is more signi�cant than the 100-day moving average and it is more signi�cant than the 50-day moving average. When AVWAPQ is greater than the 50-day MA and it is greater than the 100-day MA and it is greater than the 200-day MA, the SPY is in a strong up trend. They are all in alignment and you can see that in the chart below. Anything other than this order is less than ideal and our odds of predicting price movement is not as high. It doesn’t mean that we don’t trade, it means that we are more cautious. At the very beginning of the chart below, you can see how the MAs were all converging in the same area. Then they all started to fall into order. That con�rms that the bullish trend is underway. In the far left of the chart, please �nd the 50-day MA (light purple) and the 200-day MA (black). When the 50-day MA is above the 200-day MA the bullish market cycle begins. This is an important point. As traders we want to stay �exible, but this is the exception. Getting the market right on a longer-term basis is the single most important puzzle piece to our trading success. We have a very simple and unambiguous rule base. If we are in a bullish market cycle, our only thought is to buy dips and to add if the price action indicates aggressive buying. When the momentum slows and we approach a measured move, we will start taking gains. Once we’re in back in cash, the price action around the moving averages is going to tell us if it is time to buy. Is that support level (“safety net”) going to hold? When the market tests the 50-day MA, we want it to �y right off of it. If the market doesn’t do that, it is a sign that the selling pressure is a bit heavy. When it spends more time below the 50-day MA, it is likely to test the 100-day MA. When it does so, we want the market to �y off of the 100-day MA before it even touches it. Any cross back above the 50- day MA signals that the dip is over and that it is time to buy. If the market drops below the 100-day and it can’t rally above it quickly, it is likely to test the 200-day MA. This is a very long-term moving average. The market will rarely touch the 200-day MA during a strong up trend and any drop down to it has to be brief (one week). This is likely to be a great buying opportunity and we want the market to start blowing through all of the other moving averages with gusto. When it does so we buy and add on each successive close above another moving average. The market cycle is bullish and our only thought is to buy. The deeper the market probes for support, the better. In the chart below, look at the price action after it tests the 100 and 200-day MAs. These snap back rallies are what we want to catch and these are very high odds windows of opportunity. Look at how tight the price action is after these lows. This is what we dream of. During deep probes, we never entertain the thought of shorting. We are mentally tough. The cycle is bullish and dips are buying opportunities. Trendlines Trendlines are perhaps the oldest form of technical analysis. Any trader with a straight edge can draw them and they are easy to spot visually. Trading programs draw them using algorithms and they know where the major ones are. If you want to take a deep dive into trendlines, read the next article. If not, here are the basics. To draw them, use a log normal chart setting. Connect two highs (or lows) that stand out on the chart. The line should not penetrate the body of any candle and the angle should be no more than 45 degrees. We can draw through wicks and tails, to capture more “touches”. Trendlines take a long time to draw manually, but in this section we are only referencing the longer-term chart of SPY so it won’t take more than a few minutes a week. If the trendline is connecting the highs (H) and it is downward sloping (-), we call that a H-. If the trendline is connecting the highs (H) and it is upward sloping (+), we call that a H+. If the trendline is upward sloping (+) and it is connecting the lows (L), we call it a L+ and if it is downward sloping (-) and it is connecting the lows (L), we call it a L-. Older trendlines that span many months are more relevant than trendlines that span a few weeks. My software automatically draws trendlines. In the chart below I used a setting that allows us to see how they were drawn in the past. Normally, we only look at current trendlines that are “in range”. There might only be one or two of them and this keeps our charts clean. When the bullish cycle is just starting, there will be many breaches above H- trendlines. We want to see nice long green candles through these price points. That will serve as con�rmation that the trend is strong. We can use these breakouts and add to positions, especially if that coincides with a breakout above a major moving average. As the trend matures, we will see more H+ trendlines drawn. They will tell us where we can expect resistance. If the market blows through these levels, we can add to bullish positions. If the market struggles to get through these price points, we have to watch for tiny bodied mixed candles on light volume. That would be a sign that resistance is building and we should be in pro�t taking mode. We also want to note if these H+ trendlines are coinciding with measure moves. In the chart below you can see past “balanced” trendlines and I �nd them to be very reliable. The start and the end point are at least six months apart so they are longer-term trendlines. The distance between the starting point, the end point and the intercept have nice spacing (balanced). These breakouts served as con�rmation and we can add to bullish positions on follow through. If we are going to clutter our charts with indicators, they had better be useful. We never lose sight of the market cycle we are in, the price action and the measured moves. Our mindset during a bullish cycle is to buy dips. AVWAPQ is often the �rst line of support and I believe that trading programs reference it. If the market tests this level and it bounces off of it, we can buy that dip. We want to see immediate follow through and if we get it, we can add to the position. If the market �ounders around a support level without any “lift”, it is likely to drop to the next level of support. We let this “soft patch” run its course. It can test as many support levels as it needs to and we will not entertain shorting. We know that this drop is ultimately going to produce an excellent entry point for bullish trades and we don’t want to miss it. If the 200-day MA is tested, the market won’t spend much time there. This deep probe is likely to attract large buyers (Asset Managers) and the rebound is going to be swift and strong. As the market works its way above the other moving averages, we can add. The faster we move back above these moving averages, the better. That is the sense of urgency we are looking for. If all of the moving averages are in order (AVWAPQ > 50 > 100 > 200), the trend is very strong.

# Analysis of SPY Daily Chart — "Key Price Levels" Chapter

## 1. WHAT IS SHOWN

This is a **daily (D1) candlestick chart of SPY (SPDR S&P 500 ETF)** spanning approximately from **October 2022 through December 2024** — roughly a two-year-plus period. The current price shown is **594.78** in the upper right corner.

The chart displays a major **bullish cycle** that began in late 2022, with the price rising from roughly the 350 area to nearly 600. The overall structure shows a sustained uptrend characterized by a series of higher highs and higher lows, with periodic dips/pullbacks that get bought up.

Four moving averages are overlaid, along with a volume panel at the bottom. Several key annotations highlight the bullish cycle structure, measured move projections, and a higher-low/double-bottom formation.

---

## 2. ANNOTATIONS INVENTORY (Exhaustive)

### **Text Labels & Callouts:**

1. **"SPY - D1"** — Upper left corner, white text. Identifies the instrument and timeframe.

2. **"594.78"** — Upper right area, showing the current/last price level.

3. **"Bullish cycle begins"** — Left side of chart, with a **blue diagonal arrow** pointing down-right toward the price action around **October–November 2022**, approximately in the 350–370 range. This marks the inception point of the entire bull run.

4. **"Higher low double bottom"** — Lower-left portion of the chart, with a **blue arrow** pointing to two troughs that formed around **December 2022 to early January 2023**, approximately in the 375–380 range. The arrow curves downward to the price lows, indicating a classic higher-low/double-bottom reversal pattern that confirmed the bullish cycle.

5. **"Measured moves calculated from this peak to the trough of upcoming dip"** — Left-center area, white text with a line pointing toward a peak around **February 2023** (~415–420 area). This explains the methodology: you take the distance from a prior peak down to the next dip's trough and project that distance upward to estimate the next target.

6. **Moving Average Legend (lower right of price panel):**
   - **"Black = 200-day"** — The black line, the slowest moving average, serving as the major long-term trend indicator
   - **"Blue = 100-day"** — The blue line, intermediate-term trend
   - **"Purple = 50-day"** — The purple/violet line, shorter-term trend
   - **"Green = AVWAPQ"** — The green line, which is the **Anchored VWAP Quarterly** — a volume-weighted average price anchored to the start of each quarter

### **Drawn Lines & Zones:**

7. **Dashed blue horizontal/slightly ascending lines (measured move projections):** There are **three distinct sets of dashed blue lines** visible on the chart:

   - **First dashed line** — Extends from roughly the early 2023 area (~415–420) horizontally to the right, projecting a target zone around the **460–470 level**. This corresponds to a measured move from the Feb 2023 peak through the next dip.
   
   - **Second dashed line** — Located in the **480–500 area**, extending from roughly mid-2024, representing another measured move projection from a subsequent peak-to-trough calculation.
   
   - **Third dashed line (highest)** — Located at the top of the chart around the **590–610 area**, representing the most recent measured move projection. The price has reached and is testing this zone at the chart's right edge.

8. **Light purple/lavender shaded vertical columns:** There appear to be **approximately 4–5 shaded vertical zones** at various points along the chart. These appear to highlight significant **consolidation or breakout zones** — periods where price paused, consolidated, and then launched to higher levels. They seem to coincide with areas where the measured move projections were calculated or achieved.

9. **Moving Average Lines (overlaid on price):**
   - **Black (200-day MA):** The slowest, smoothest line. It turns from flat/declining to rising around early-mid 2023 and has remained in a steady upward slope since. Price has stayed consistently above it for the majority of the bull run.
   - **Blue (100-day MA):** Tracks closer to price than the 200-day. It turned up earlier and has served as support on several pullbacks.
   - **Purple (50-day MA):** The most reactive to price, closest to the candles. It has acted as the first line of dynamic support during shallow pullbacks.
   - **Green (AVWAPQ):** The quarterly anchored VWAP weaves through price action, resetting each quarter. It tends to track near the 50-day MA and provides context for institutional positioning relative to the quarter's average price.

10. **Volume panel (bottom):** Shows red and blue/green volume bars. Notable volume spikes appear at key turning points — particularly around the October 2022 lows, during breakout periods (corresponding to the shaded zones), and during some of the pullbacks.

---

## 3. PATTERN OR CONCEPT BEING TAUGHT

### **Primary Concept: Bullish Market Cycle Structure & Measured Moves as Key Price Levels**

This chart teaches traders how to identify and navigate a **long-term bullish cycle** using:

#### **A. Bullish Cycle Identification:**
- The cycle begins with a **higher low / double bottom** formation (Oct–Dec 2022) — a failed attempt to make new lows that signals a shift from bearish to bullish sentiment.
- Confirmation comes when price breaks above prior resistance and the moving averages begin to stack bullishly (50-day above 100-day above 200-day).

#### **B. Measured Move Projections:**
The core technique taught is:

> **"When price forms a peak and then pulls back to a trough (dip), measure that distance (peak-to-trough). Project that same distance upward from the peak to estimate the next price target/key level."**

This creates upside **price targets** that serve as key resistance/profit-taking levels. The chart shows this methodology applied **multiple times** throughout the bull cycle, with each successive measured move projection being reached and often exceeded.

#### **C. Moving Average Confluence as Support:**
The rule here is:

> **"When price is above all major moving averages (50, 100, 200-day) and they are stacked in bullish order (50 > 100 > 200), the trend is firmly bullish. Pullbacks to these moving averages — especially the 50-day and 100-day — represent buying
